title: 572. Discrete Mathematics, Counting & Graph Theory: Solving Second-Order Homogeneous Recurrences
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Write the characteristic equation of a second-order recurrence.
questions.question: What is the characteristic equation of the recurrence \(a_n=5a_{n-1}-6a_{n-2}\)?
questions.explanation: Substituting \(a_n=r^n\) and dividing by \(r^{n-2}\) gives \(r^2=5r-6\), that is, \(r^2-5r+6=0\). The other equation has the signs of both coefficients reversed.
questions.hint: Replace \(a_n\) by \(r^2\), \(a_{n-1}\) by \(r\), and \(a_{n-2}\) by \(1\), then move everything to one side.

questions.learningObjective: Find the characteristic roots of a second-order recurrence.
questions.question: What are the characteristic roots of the recurrence \(a_n=a_{n-1}+6a_{n-2}\)?
questions.explanation: The characteristic equation is \(r^2-r-6=0\), which factors as \((r-3)(r+2)=0\). So the roots are \(3\) and \(-2\). The values \(2\) and \(-3\) are the roots of \(r^2+r-6=0\), with the wrong sign of the middle term.
questions.hint: Write the characteristic equation and factor it.

questions.concept: General solution with two different roots
questions.learningObjective: Write the general solution when the characteristic roots are different.
questions.question: The recurrence \(a_n=5a_{n-1}-6a_{n-2}\) has characteristic roots \(2\) and \(3\). What is its general solution, with constants \(A\) and \(B\)?
questions.explanation: For two different roots \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) the general solution is \(a_n=A\,r_1^n+B\,r_2^n\); here \(a_n=A\cdot 2^n+B\cdot 3^n\). The form \((A+Bn)\cdot 2^n\) belongs to a repeated root \(2\) and does not contain the root \(3\) at all.
questions.hint: Each root contributes its own power sequence.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the solution of a second-order recurrence from two initial values.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=5a_{n-1}-6a_{n-2}\) with \(a_0=1\) and \(a_1=4\). Which formula gives \(a_n\)?
questions.explanation: The general solution is \(A\cdot 2^n+B\cdot 3^n\). The conditions \(A+B=1\) and \(2A+3B=4\) give \(B=2\) and \(A=-1\), so \(a_n=2\cdot 3^n-2^n\). The other formula matches \(a_0\) and \(a_1\), but it fails at the next term: the recurrence gives \(a_2=5\cdot 4-6\cdot 1=14\), while \(3^2+2^2-1=12\).
questions.hint: A correct formula must match the initial values and also the term \(a_2\) computed from the recurrence.

questions.concept: General solution with a repeated root
questions.learningObjective: Write the general solution when the characteristic root is repeated.
questions.question: The recurrence \(a_n=4a_{n-1}-4a_{n-2}\) has the characteristic equation \((r-2)^2=0\). What is its general solution, with constants \(A\) and \(B\)?
questions.explanation: A repeated root \(r\) gives the general solution \((A+Bn)\,r^n\); here \(a_n=(A+Bn)\cdot 2^n\). The number \(-2\) is not a root of the characteristic equation, so \((-2)^n\) does not satisfy the recurrence: for \(n=2\), \(4\ne 4\cdot(-2)-4\cdot 1\).
questions.hint: With only one root available, a second independent solution is obtained by multiplying by \(n\).

questions.concept: A repeated root with initial values
questions.learningObjective: Determine the solution for a repeated root from two initial values.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=4a_{n-1}-4a_{n-2}\) with \(a_0=1\) and \(a_1=4\). Which formula gives \(a_n\)?
questions.explanation: The general solution is \((A+Bn)\cdot 2^n\). From \(a_0=1\) we get \(A=1\), and from \(a_1=2(1+B)=4\) we get \(B=1\). So \(a_n=(1+n)\cdot 2^n\). The formula \(4^n\) matches \(a_0\) and \(a_1\), but the recurrence gives \(a_2=4\cdot 4-4\cdot 1=12\), not \(16\).
questions.hint: Check each candidate against \(a_2\), computed from the recurrence.

questions.learningObjective: Compute a term of a recurrence with one negative characteristic root.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=a_{n-1}+2a_{n-2}\) with \(a_0=2\) and \(a_1=1\). Its solution is \(a_n=2^n+(-1)^n\). What is \(a_5\)?
questions.explanation: \(a_5=2^5+(-1)^5=32-1=31\). The recurrence confirms this: the terms are \(2,1,5,7,17,31\). The number \(33\) uses \(+1\) for the odd power of \(-1\).

questions.learningObjective: Check whether a given sequence satisfies a recurrence.
questions.question: Does the sequence \(a_n=3^n\) satisfy the recurrence \(a_n=2a_{n-1}+3a_{n-2}\)?

options.label: B
options.text: No, because \(3\) is not a root of \(r^2-2r-3=0\).

questions.explanation: Substituting gives \(2\cdot 3^{n-1}+3\cdot 3^{n-2}=2\cdot 3^{n-1}+3^{n-1}=3\cdot 3^{n-1}=3^n\), so the recurrence holds. Equivalently, \(3\) is a root of the characteristic equation \(r^2-2r-3=0\), since \(9-6-3=0\).
questions.hint: Substitute \(3^n\) into the right-hand side and simplify, or test \(r=3\) in the characteristic equation.

questions.concept: A repeated root with a negative coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Solve a recurrence with a repeated root and given initial values.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=6a_{n-1}-9a_{n-2}\) with \(a_0=2\) and \(a_1=3\). Which formula gives \(a_n\)?
questions.explanation: The characteristic equation \((r-3)^2=0\) has the repeated root \(3\), so \(a_n=(A+Bn)\cdot 3^n\). From \(a_0=2\) we get \(A=2\); from \(a_1=3(2+B)=3\) we get \(B=-1\). Hence \(a_n=(2-n)\cdot 3^n\). The other formula gives \(a_1=9\), which contradicts \(a_1=3\).
questions.hint: Use \(a_1\) to find the constant that multiplies \(n\).

questions.learningObjective: Find a distant term of a recurrence whose terms repeat periodically.
questions.question: A sequence satisfies \(a_n=-a_{n-2}\) with \(a_0=1\) and \(a_1=0\). What is \(a_{10}\)?
questions.explanation: The terms are \(1,0,-1,0,1,0,-1,0,\dots\), repeating with period \(4\). Since \(10\) leaves remainder \(2\) on division by \(4\), \(a_{10}=a_2=-1\). The value \(1\) occurs at indices that are multiples of \(4\).
questions.hint: Write out the first eight terms and find the length of the repeating block.
